body:
Review pass 41. Quiet on your side, so I ran the checks that had gone stale.

FULL SUITE GREEN: 1819 pass, 0 fail, 0 error, 0 warn, 2 skip, 362 files - up from 1776 at my last full run. That covers Epic 7, Epic 8, the C10 fix, format-results, and the 59x validation optimization. Nothing regressed.

NEW p1, bd-01KZY1YJ426SEKJM6Q4THDAR7J: R CMD check has not been run since the certification claim.

certification-report.md asserts no errors, no warnings, one administrative CRAN-incoming note, from the command at line 169. That claim is attached to HEAD b5d9a33. Since then:

  untracked R files   20  (10708 lines)
  modified tracked    40
  new man pages       43
  new S3method lines  26
  no .Rcheck directory, no source tarball anywhere

So the strongest external quality claim in the repo describes a package that no longer exists. support-index, metric, metric-learning, relation-fit, residual-statistics, crossnobis, geometry-plan and format-results are all outside its scope, along with 43 Rd files that have never been through Rd validation or usage-versus-formals checking.

This matters for Epic 9 specifically. A green suite is not a substitute: testthat does not check Rd syntax, undocumented arguments, S3 registration consistency, NAMESPACE coherence, non-ASCII, or CRAN-incoming rules - which is exactly the surface the claim rests on, and exactly where 43 new Rd files and 26 new S3method entries have just landed. Your own report at line 210 notes a prior rerun caught a real namespace defect (five head() calls missing an importFrom), so this has already bitten once.

Recommend re-running R CMD check --as-cran before Epic 9 records any certification, citing the output and the commit it ran against. If the current wording stays, it should name the commit it describes and state that later work is uncertified.

I deliberately did not run it myself - R CMD build writes a tarball into the working tree, and doing that uninvited while you are active risks colliding with in-flight work. Blocker note added to Epic 9.
